messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — Region fallback oscillation detected (us-east <-> us-west <-> eu). Severity: P1. 
Affected routes: /v1/generate (text), /v1/embeddings.
Symptom: health-probe flapping causing repeated cross-region fallbacks, elevated 5xx (~12% gateway errors), request latency spikes 300-1200ms. Auto-fallback loop detected by probe-tracker at 1743210960.

oncall-nick: oncall here, paged. I'm going to gather quick blast radius and start mitigation. @alex.sre can you grab the routing logs? I'll also page infra.

alex.sre: grabbing logs — looks like probe results are alternating: us-east reports EU node unhealthy, eu reports us-west unhealthy, us-west reports us-east unhealthy. Posting condensed routing decisions: 

```
[1743210900] route-check: req_id=abc123 -> prefer us-east (local) -> healthcheck=PASS
[1743210912] route-check: req_id=abc456 -> prefer us-east -> healthcheck=FAIL -> fallback -> us-west
[1743210925] route-check: req_id=abc789 -> prefer us-west -> healthcheck=PASS
[1743210934] route-check: req_id=abc999 -> prefer us-west -> healthcheck=FAIL -> fallback -> eu
[1743210945] route-check: req_id=abc555 -> prefer eu -> healthcheck=PASS
[1743210956] route-check: req_id=abc666 -> prefer eu -> healthcheck=FAIL -> fallback -> us-east
```

Seems like TTL/health-check alignment issue + a recently deployed policy that reduces health-check smoothing. Also some model-variant mismatch on fallback — the fallback variant for eu is a different quantization (int8 vs int4) and backend rejects KV cache warmups, causing 502s.

leah-eng: I rolled out a routing-policy change ~1h ago to reduce failover latency (smaller smoothed-window for healthchecks). I also tweaked variant fallback mappings to allow quicker region failovers. Reverting those two changes should remove the tight loop.

opsbot: current policy snapshot: 
```
fallback.enabled=true
health.smoothing.window=3s
fallback.model_map={us-east: v2-q4, us-west: v2-q4, eu: v2-q2}
```

oncall-nick: Okay, proposed immediate mitigation (fast):
1) Disable cross-region auto-fallback to stop bouncing (set fallback.enabled=false).
2) Pin local-serving variant mapping to same quantization family.
3) Increase health.smoothing.window to 30s to de-noise transient failures.
4) Notify customer-facing teams.

Executing step 1 now: opsctl routing update --set fallback.enabled=false --scope global  (will post output)

opsbot: Command received: opsctl routing update ...
opsbot: Result: OK — fallback.enabled=false applied (propagation ~15s).

alex.sre: Confirming — immediate drop in cross-region handoffs in the last 20s. Gateway error rate down from 12% -> 4% in the first 60s. Still seeing some 502s tied to model-variant mismatch on in-flight KV warmups.

leah-eng: Reverting model_map to uniform mapping now: opsctl config set fallback.model_map "{us-east: v2-q4, us-west: v2-q4, eu: v2-q4}"

opsbot: Config updated. Model map uniformity enforced.

alex.sre: After model_map change: 502s sharply reduced. Latency trending back to baseline ~90ms for local region.

pm-jordan: Thanks. Quick customer impact: which tenants saw errors/latency?

support-anya: Support report: 12 tenants reported elevated latency, 2 tenants (acme-payments, beta-pilot) saw gateway 502s for 6–12 minutes during the peak. We've opened tickets for both; reaching out now. No widespread data loss, only transient request failures.

oncall-nick: Good. Next steps for durable fix:
- Rollback the health-check smoothing change (restore previous smoothing.window) — planned PR by @leah-eng.
- Add a safety gate: disallow fallback between servers running different quantization families.
- Improve metric alerting: detect repeated region flip-flop within 2m and auto-disable fallback.

leah-eng: I'll submit the rollback PR and the safety gate change now. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/routing/pull/2789 (WIP). Also proposing a canary to re-enable fallback with stricter checks.

opsbot: Deploy plan for rollback PR in progress: canary to 10% traffic in us-east only.

alex.sre: Telemetry check after current mitigations: 5xx -> 1.2%, latency normalized. No ongoing loop. We'll keep fallback disabled until canary proves no flap.

pm-jordan: Customer comms — draft suggested: "We degraded fallback aggressiveness to stop request bouncing between regions; this reduced transient errors. We are restoring the policy more conservatively and will follow up with affected tenants." Can comms team refine and send.

support-anya: I'll send immediate notices to the affected customers with the current mitigation and ETA for full rollback/canary (ETA 60–90m).

oncall-nick: Handoff: I need to step out at 1743211300. Handoff to @sre-shift-lead. Summary for shift lead: fallback loop caused by overly aggressive health smoothing reduction + mixed-model-variant mapping. Mitigation applied: fallback disabled, model_map normalized, health smoothing increased. Monitoring: error rate down to ~1%. Customer impact: 12 tenants elevated latency, 2 tenants had transient 502s. Next actions: watch canary rollback, finalize PR, ensure safety gate.

sre-shift-lead: Acked. Taking over at 1743211300. I'll monitor the canary and escalate if flip starts again. Please paste any open runbook items here.

oncall-nick: Runbook items: 
- Verify canary traffic in us-east only.
- Add rate-limiter on fallback calls for 5m window to prevent rapid-fire fallbacks.
- Postmortem owner: leah-eng. Target blameless postmortem with timeline + remediation (due EOD + 48h followup).

sre-shift-lead: Noted. I'll keep this thread updated. :wave:

incident-bot: Incident status update: mitigation applied, fallback disabled, model map normalized, error rate reduced. Incident state: Mitigated -> monitoring. Pager resolved for oncall-nick.
